answer: Graph-conductance filtering resists Sybil attacks by gating new agents at a vouching inlet before granting auction access. Verifiers run short random walks from a vetted summit of seed keys, scoring nodes by landing probability to form a quartz barrier against isolated clones. Attackers incur the verifiable cost of earning interaction history or bribing peers per identity to forge attack edges. However, adversaries can still breach the cut by buying aged accounts or forming covert endorsement rings.
